guide.immersive_smithing.getting_started:
## Your first workshop
Start with stone tongs, a stone hammer, a forge, an anvil and a water trough. Most metal equipment is made here, by hand, instead of at a crafting table.

## 1. Plan and heat
Melt metal in the forge's basin over a lit fire. Open the pattern book on the forge's rim, pin what you want to make, and commit it at the billet tray with empty tongs. Pump the bellows and turn the billet until it glows evenly, then draw it out.

## 2. Shape
Lay it on the anvil. Strike the chalk-marked parts with a hammer, in order; turn it over when a part is on the other face. Reheat it on the forge's rest if it cools.

## 3. Quench and fit
Lower it into the trough with tongs and lift it when the hiss subsides. If it needs a handle or straps, fit them at the anvil, then take your finished piece.
guide.immersive_smithing.smiths_forge.te:
## Load and light
Metal goes in the basin at the back of the top, fuel in the firebox below. Ignite the fuel; the metal melts into the basin. Between heats the fire banks: once nothing is heating and the fuel burning has burnt down, it stays lit for a minute without using fuel, so a piece put back on the rest lights the next fuel by itself. Sneak-use with an empty hand takes back unmelted metal (top) or unlit fuel (bottom).

## Its working parts
The billet tray at the front of the top, the bellows on the right with its handle, the reheat rest across the mouth of the fire, the pattern book on the left rim and the components of a committed job on the right rim. Each is used where it is.

## Breaking it
A forge with molten metal or a billet on its tray cannot be broken in survival. Cast the metal or cancel the job first.
guide.immersive_smithing.fuels_and_ignit:
## Solid fuel
Right-click the lower half with fuel: logs, planks, wooden slabs, sticks, coal, charcoal or coal blocks. Then ignite it with Flint and Steel or a Fire Charge. The fire only burns while there is metal to melt.

## Lava
Lava is different: pour a lava bucket into the lower half and it heats the forge straight away, with no ignition. An empty bucket scoops a full bucket back out.

## Recover unused fuel
Sneak-use with an empty hand on the lower half to take back fuel that is not burning.
guide.immersive_smithing.material_famili:
## One family per forge
Every metal belongs to a material family: iron, gold, copper, netherite, and metals from other mods found through their forge:ingots tags.

## Material units
Items are worth material units: a nugget is 1, an ingot or raw ore is 9 and a storage block is 81. Each item costs units, so an iron sword needs 18 (two ingots) plus a stick.

## Melting speed
Families melt at different speeds. Gold melts quickly, netherite slowly.
## Carry hot metal
Tongs commit and draw billets and carry workpieces between the forge, anvil, rest and trough. A carried piece cools in the air, but only while you are carrying it in a loaded world; it never cools while you are offline.

## Dropped tongs
If you drop the tongs or die, the workpiece stays in them, and anyone can pick them up and carry on.

## Recycle a workpiece
Sneak-use loaded tongs on the forge's basin, twice, to melt the workpiece back: its progress is lost, its recoverable metal returns, and components not yet fitted come back to you.
guide.immersive_smithing.smiths_anvil.te:
## Place and retrieve
Use loaded tongs on the anvil to set the piece down, and empty tongs to pick it up. The anvil holds one piece, or one finished item waiting to be taken. While someone works at it, nobody else can take the piece.

## If the anvil breaks
The piece drops as a Hot Workpiece item with all its progress. Use empty tongs in the air to pick it up, or place it on another anvil.

## Repairs and names
The Smith's Anvil does not repair or rename items; that is still the vanilla anvil's job.
guide.immersive_smithing.smiths_trough.t:
## Fill with water
Use water buckets on the trough. One bucket gives four quenches by default. Pipes can also supply water.

## Quench
Hold the shaped piece in tongs and lower it in. Keep it under while it hisses; when the hiss subsides and the steam clears, lift it with empty tongs. Anything from the end of the hiss to a while after is a perfect quench.

## Interruptions
Lifted before it touches the water, nothing is used. Lifted early, it keeps its progress: lower it again to finish (more dips cost a little quality). A piece left in very long cools completely.
guide.immersive_smithing.makers_mark.tex:
## Every piece knows its smith
A finished piece records who completed it: hover over it and it says Crafted by you. The mark stays through repairs, enchanting, dyeing and elemental upgrades; only melting the piece down removes it.

## Title and inscription
Engrave it whenever you like: sneak-use a Smith's Anvil with the finished piece in hand to give it a title and up to three lines. A stamp rings out on the anvil. Faulty work cannot be signed.

## Found gear
Equipment from chests and treasure carries an honest grade of its own, never better than Standard, so a Fine or Masterwork piece was always made by a smith.
guide.immersive_smithing.equipment_quali:
## Forge: durability
Smithed items carry two scores. The Forge score comes from how well the billet was heated (most of it) and from the quench, and sets durability: at 50 an item lasts as long as usual, at 100 it lasts a quarter longer and at 0 a quarter less.

## Anvil: efficacy
The Anvil score comes from the shaping: every required part, the heat each blow was struck at, the right kind of blow, and marks left behind. It sets efficacy: attack damage for weapons, mining speed for tools and armour points for armour. At 100 it is fifteen percent better.

The overall label averages both: Crude (below 35), Standard (35 to 69), Fine (70 to 89) and Masterwork (90 and above). Hold Shift over an item for details.
guide.immersive_smithing.faulty_equipmen:
## What Faulty means
Faulty items work, but poorly: by default half the durability and seventy percent of the efficacy. New work only becomes Faulty when the server enables burning: metal held far too hot for too long burns, with a warning first. Pieces from before this update keep the grade they had.

## How to recover
The Smith's Grindstone cannot fix them. Melt them down and forge again instead.
guide.immersive_smithing.reforging.title: Reforging
guide.immersive_smithing.reforging.text:
## Recover the metal
Metal equipment the forge recognises can go back into a forge of its family: enchanted, Faulty or anything in between. By default all of its metal is recovered.

## What is lost
Enchantments, quality, custom names and repair history are lost when it melts. Datapacks can mark special items as not recyclable. An unfinished workpiece is recycled only on purpose: sneak-use the basin twice.
guide.immersive_smithing.casting.title: Casting
guide.immersive_smithing.casting.text:
## Cast ingots
Open the pattern book on a ready forge. Above the patterns, the Cast panel turns free molten metal back into ingots: 9 units make one. Choose how many with - and + (Shift steps by 10) or All; the line below shows exactly what you get. Press Cast. Metal reserved by a committed job is never cast.

## Nuggets and remainders
Metal that does not make a whole ingot stays molten. Cast it as nuggets where the metal has them, or add more of the same metal. Copper and netherite have no nuggets.

## Nothing else changes
Casting needs no fuel and gives no quality, maker's mark or experience. The items go straight into your inventory, and casting stops when it is full.
guide.immersive_smithing.smiths_grindsto:
## Rest a piece at the wheel
Use the grindstone while holding a finished, smithed piece: it rests by the wheel and the price of one pass is shown. Switch between durability and efficacy with your use button in the work view or the Next part key.

## Hold it to the wheel
Hold the edge to the turning wheel (hold use, or click in the work view) for one pass. The XP is only charged, and the score raised by 5, when the pass completes; lift it early and nothing happens. Higher scores cost more levels; the limit is 100.

## Take it back
Sneak-use with an empty hand. A piece that was never graded starts from Standard. Faulty items cannot be refined.
guide.immersive_smithing.tool_tiers.text:
## Durability and recovery
Tongs and hammers come in stone, iron, diamond and netherite. Better tools last longer and hammers recover slightly faster between blows.

## Skill still matters
They never add quality on their own: a careful smith makes Masterwork equipment with stone tools. Repair them with their material at an anvil. Unbreaking and Mending work on them.
guide.immersive_smithing.netherite.title: Netherite
guide.immersive_smithing.netherite.text:
## Forge directly
Netherite equipment is forged directly from netherite ingots; no smithing template or diamond equipment is needed. A netherite sword costs 18 netherite units (two ingots) and a stick; armour costs 36 (boots) to 72 (chestplate) units, and is listed dimmed with what it still needs while the forge holds less.

## Modded upgrades
The same goes for other mods' smithing-table upgrades, such as netherite shields and weapons: they are forged from the metal, in the shape of the item they used to upgrade, and the smithing-table recipe is disabled.

## Lava required
Netherite only melts with lava as the heat source, so pour a lava bucket into the forge. Lava needs no ignition.
guide.immersive_smithing.modded_equipmen:
## Finding modded metals
Immersive Smithing finds metals from other mods through their forge:ingots, nuggets, storage_blocks and raw_materials tags, and studies the crafting recipes of weapons, tools, armor and metal shields.

## Recipe detection
When a weapon, tool or armor piece is made mostly of one metal (the one it is repaired with), its recipe becomes a smithing recipe and that recipe is disabled. Sticks, leather and small fittings of another metal are components taken from your inventory. A metal shield built on a wooden base shield only needs the metal: the base is not required. A recipe that only reshapes a finished piece, such as a sword made into a spear, still works at the crafting table and keeps the piece's quality. Recipes that mix two metals, or are otherwise unclear, are skipped and still crafted normally. Datapacks can add or override anything.

## Spartan Weaponry
Spartan Weaponry is supported out of the box: every metal weapon, including throwing weapons, longbows and heavy crossbows, has its own recipe and anvil pattern. The studded club and cestus need only their iron. Arrows and bolts are still crafted. A thrown weapon keeps its quality in flight, and arrows share the quality of the bow or crossbow that fires them.

## Epic Fight and Simply Swords
Epic Fight's metal weapons come with built-in forge recipes that need no setup: a longsword or tachi is four ingots and a stick, a greatsword six ingots and a plank, a spear two ingots and three sticks, and the uchigatana four iron ingots with a diamond, two leather and a stick. Netherite weapons are forged from netherite directly. The wooden bokken is crafted from two planks and a stick, laid diagonally. Simply Swords' metal weapons are found automatically and forged on an anvil pattern of their shape. Quality counts once, in either hand and in Epic Fight's battle mode, and Simply Swords' abilities and thrown weapons use it too. Runic weapons, rerolls and unique weapons are still made or found the way their mod intends. Found weapons can carry quality and be refined at the grindstone, and unique weapons can't be melted down.

## Epic Knights
Epic Knights and its add-ons are supported out of the box. Their metal weapons, armor and shields are forged, each on an anvil pattern of its shape, and the crafting recipes they replace are disabled. Steel plates and the other metal plates melt down for one ingot. Gilded, blackened and other pieces made from a finished piece are still made that way, and keep its quality. Opening or closing a helmet's visor keeps its quality too. Wooden and leather pieces are crafted as before. Relics and other found pieces are never forged, and relics can't be melted down. If no mod in the pack provides a piece's metal, such as bronze or silver, its usual recipe stays.

Server operators can switch each of these integrations off in the server config.
guide.immersive_smithing.automation.text:
## Feed your stations
Hoppers and pipes can feed metal into the top and sides of a forge, fuel into its bottom and back, and water into a trough.

## Work by hand
Automation can never pin a pattern, commit a job, heat or draw a billet, shape, quench or fit: every item is made by a smith. Comparators read the forge and the trough.
guide.immersive_smithing.jei.title: JEI
guide.immersive_smithing.jei.text:
## Browse recipes
With Just Enough Items installed, every smithing recipe, including those detected from other mods, appears in the Smithing category. It shows the metal, the components, the anvil pattern and the Forge, Anvil and Trough steps.

## Replaced recipes
Crafting recipes that smithing replaced are not shown. Recipes it keeps, such as one that reshapes a finished piece, still appear in their usual categories.
guide.immersive_smithing.troubleshooting:
## Nothing to commit
Make sure the metal has melted (the basin glows) and a pattern is pinned: use the book on the rim. The pinned drawing beside the tray shows what will be made.

## Patterns listed dimmed
Patterns you cannot make yet are dimmed with what they still need: more metal, a component such as sticks, or a requirement of another mod.

## The piece will not shape
It is too cold (reheat it on the forge's rest), the part is on the other face (turn it over), or another part must be done first. The status says which.

## Missing modded item
An operator can run /immersivesmithing report, /immersivesmithing process and /immersivesmithing recipe <item> to see why. After changing the server config, run /immersivesmithing reload.

guide.immersive_smithing.epic_knights.te:
Metal equipment follows the loaded native recipes. A structural upgrade consumes the exact base, added metal and every fitting. The knight chestplate needs a halfarmor chestplate and 45 steel units (five plates). Forge and anvil scores and the maker are renewed; supported names, enchantments, decorations and proportional wear survive.

Rings and mail have fractional metal content. The forge rounds the final charge up once; recycling rounds known content down. Minor plating and other materials are not returned. Direct melting of fractional components is unavailable.

Gilding, darkening, dyes, heraldry, trims, attachments, ammunition and alloys keep their native processes. Cosmetic changes keep quality and the original maker. Visors use the native swap; rare gear keeps its original acquisition. Shields retain native blocking, and horse armor retains native protection.

Fire or unload guns before upgrading or melting them; refinement keeps the loaded stack intact. Supported shots use the firing weapon’s quality once, without changing loading or ammunition. Overgeared, TerraFirma and TerraFirmaGreg bridges retain their own manufacturing and equipment effects.

guide.immersive_smithing.pattern_book.te:
## Plan without spending
Use the book on the forge's rim (or empty tongs on a ready forge with nothing pinned). Patterns you can make now come first; the rest are dimmed with exactly what they need. Search by name, or @mod for one mod; Tab changes the category; F or right-click stars a favourite. Choosing one pins it beside the tray. Nothing is reserved yet.

## Commit
Use the billet tray with empty tongs. Now the metal is reserved and the exact components leave your inventory, and a dark billet is cast on the tray. Sneak-use the tray with an empty hand twice to cancel before drawing: the metal is free again and the components come back.

## Again
The pattern stays pinned, so the next piece needs only another commit at the tray.
guide.immersive_smithing.heating_the_bil:
## Air and fire
A lit fire alone brings the billet only to a low working heat. Each stroke of the bellows drives the fire hotter for a few seconds. Watch the colour: dark, red, cherry, orange, yellow. The status names the heat in words too.

## Even heat
The middle of the tray is hottest. Turn (move) the billet with tongs so both ends get their share. An uneven billet still draws, but heats worse.

## Draw it out
When even its coolest part is workable, draw it out with empty tongs. How well it was heated is recorded now and becomes most of its durability. Overheating builds scale that costs quality; hammering knocks some of it off again.
guide.immersive_smithing.shaping.title: Shaping
guide.immersive_smithing.shaping.text:
## Strike the marks
Chalk marks outline what is left to do: draw out a blade, punch an eye, spread a bit, dish a plate. Aim at a marked part and strike. Where inside the part you hit does not matter; doing the right part, in order, at the right heat does.

## Heat and blows
Metal below working heat does not move: reheat it on the forge's rest, and all its shaping stays. With empty tongs in a hand you can lift the piece off, or set a carried one down, from the anvil's work view. At the ideal heat every blow is clean. Hold the heavy-blow key for rough work (drawing, spreading, punching); a heavy blow mars finishing work.

## Turn it over
Some parts are on the other face: turn the piece over with the turn key or a right-click. Finished parts saturate: more blows there only leave marks. A few clean blows at the ideal heat smooth marks out.
guide.immersive_smithing.fitting.title: Fitting Components
guide.immersive_smithing.fitting.text:
## After the quench
A piece that needs a handle, straps or other parts comes out of the trough cooled but unfinished. Lay it on the anvil: the components you committed with it wait on the tray beside it.

## Fit
Use the anvil with an empty hand (or the work view) to fit each component into its marked socket. With the last one the finished item appears on the anvil: take it. Pieces without components are finished as they leave the water.
guide.immersive_smithing.work_views.text:
## Three views
Cinematic moves the camera to a framed view of the station; Shoulder stays near your own view; World view never moves the camera. All three use the same rules and reach the same quality. Change it in the client config, or bind the Cycle work view key.

## In a work view
Point at a part and click, or choose parts with the arrow keys and press Space. Your attack button acts, your use button is the second action, the turn-over key turns a piece. Escape, a movement key or the Work at station key leave at once. Chat and the inventory open over the view.

## Comfort
Reduced motion cuts instead of moving the camera. Particles, flashes, work sounds, high-contrast guides and larger marks have their own options. Heat and progress are always also named in words.
